text1: The Toranaga-class autonomous cruiser was conceived near the end of the Domain's expansion as a strategic expeditionary flagship: a warship able to survey, secure, and reclaim frontier systems without waiting for fleet support. Its compact frame carries capital-grade flux architecture, exceptional omni-shielding, two integrated support bays, and an unusually complete logistics suite for long independent operations. Only one prototype is believed to have completed trials before the Collapse ended the program, leaving the Toranaga as a singular artifact of Domain engineering without compromise.

The DiAnn-class destroyer was developed as the fast escort counterpart to the Toranaga program: a compact superiority warship able to keep pace with advanced strategic cruisers and break enemy formations before they could threaten the flagship. Its high-output reactor, efficient omni-shield, dense energy armament, and two integrated support bays gave it combat reach far beyond ordinary destroyers. Production remained extremely limited, not because the design failed, but because its reactor and field-control systems were too complex for wartime mass manufacture before the Collapse ended the program.

The RayChen-class frigate was the Toranaga program's answer to a simple question: how far could frigate performance be pushed if cost, maintainability, and production scale were ignored. Its compact frame wraps prototype-grade flux architecture, high-efficiency omni-shields, and precision thruster control around a small set of overpowered forward weapons. The result is not a miniature cruiser, but a duelist built to choose the terms of every engagement and end them before heavier ships can respond.

The Hahn-class frigate emerged from the same design brief as the RayChen, pursued along a parallel line of development within the Toranaga program. Where its sibling committed every mount to fixed forward energy fire, the Hahn's rounder hull carries a pair of forward strike missiles alongside tracking energy turrets, letting it open an engagement with a decisive alpha strike before settling into sustained pressure. Its shield generator sits fractionally off-center in its housing, a quirk of the prototype's field-control architecture that pilots learn to use rather than fight. Like the RayChen, only a handful of Hahn prototypes are believed to have existed before the Collapse ended the program.
